overlap.title: The census contribution is a fixed amount
overlap.summary: Those counted from age twenty owe the same half-shekel contribution.
overlap.reasoning: The contribution is explicitly fixed, rather than proportional to wealth. The plague language is a religious claim within the law, not an independently demonstrated causal link.
overlap.scope: This does not establish historical collection rates, modern monetary value or an empirically tested way of preventing disease.

overlap.title: Voluntary gifts and a fixed census payment are separate contributions
overlap.summary: Willing donations coexist with a uniform census contribution; excess gifts are stopped.
overlap.reasoning: Willingness governs the donation descriptions; a specified amount governs those counted. Treating every sanctuary contribution as one identical payment would create a misleading conflict.
overlap.scope: The narrative distinguishes funding categories. It does not independently verify the donor list, census total, material inventory or how obligations were administered.

overlap.title: Construction repeats selected earlier specifications

overlap.title: The military census is not a count of everyone
overlap.summary: The 603,550 total counts eligible males from age twenty and excludes the Levites.
overlap.reasoning: Internal agreement of these totals does not independently verify the ancient population. Treating the number as the size of the whole traveling community overlooks the census criteria.
overlap.scope: The population scale, Hebrew numerical terminology, chronology and archaeological evidence need separate investigation. No demographic multiplier or historical certification is supplied here.

overlap.title: Royal orders and the rescue of children
overlap.summary: The midwives refuse Pharaoh’s order to kill boys; Pharaoh’s daughter later rescues a Hebrew child.
overlap.reasoning: The two chapters contrast royal policy with the choices of named midwives and a member of the royal household. Reading them together shows that the narrative does not portray every Egyptian as carrying out the king’s order.

overlap.title: Wind and locust migration
overlap.summary: Wind-driven locust movement fits observed swarm behavior; it does not verify this particular plague.
overlap.reasoning: Wind-assisted migration is an independently documented biological behavior. This supports that limited feature of the description, rather than the entire sequence of events.
overlap.scope: FAO’s observations do not identify the species in this ancient account, date the event, verify its unprecedented scale or confirm divine timing and the complete removal of every locust.
